ch24.d.preset: Starting arrangement of the charges (drag to move; the tray at the lower left adds and removes)
ch24.d.view: Show the potential as equipotential lines, a colour map (vermilion +, blue −), or both
ch24.d.lines: Also draw faint electric field lines
ch24.d.dV: Potential difference $\Delta V$ between neighbouring equipotentials
ch24.goal.V: Potential $V$: potential energy per unit charge; the work done by the field, $W = -q_0\Delta V$, does not depend on the path
ch24.goal.perp: Equipotentials cross field lines at right angles; $\vec E$ points where the potential drops fastest ($\vec E = -\nabla V$)
ch24.obs.along: Drag the test charge $q_0$ along an equipotential: $\Delta V \approx 0$, $W \approx 0$
ch24.obs.cross: Drag across the equipotentials: each line crossed changes $\Delta V$ by one step, and $W = -q_0\Delta V$
ch24.obs.path: Different paths from A to the same point give the same $W$; back at the start, $W = 0$ (drag A to start a new path)
ch24.obs.spacing: Where equipotentials are close together the field is strong, $E \approx \Delta V / \Delta s$
ch24.obs.heat: Colour map: vermilion (+) near positive charges, blue (−) near negative ones; the mid-plane of a dipole is $V = 0$ (dashed)
ch24.obs.edit: Moving a charge recomputes $W$ along the path already drawn, in the new field
ch24.as.units: Charges in nC, lengths in m, test charge $q_0 = +1$ nC, so $W$ is in nJ
ch24.as.levels: Equipotentials are drawn for $\lvert V \rvert \le 12\,\Delta V$. Map colours are compressed as $\tanh(V/25\,\mathrm{V})$
ch24.as.num: $W$ integrates $q_0\vec E\cdot d\vec s$ numerically along the dragged path; $\Delta V$ is the potential difference of its end points
